question: The cornerstone of treatment is:

options.A: Complete en bloc gross resection as a single specimen with involved organs

correctAnswerText: Complete en bloc gross resection as a single specimen with involved organs
explanation: Complete en bloc gross resection is the cornerstone, aiming at a macroscopically complete single specimen [1].
sourceArticle: Management of Primary Retroperitoneal Sarcoma (RPS) in the Adult: An Updated Consensus Approach from the Transatlantic Australasian RPS Working Group

question: The standard biopsy is:

options.A: Image-guided coaxial core needle biopsy, 14–18 gauge

correctAnswerText: Image-guided coaxial core needle biopsy, 14–18 gauge
explanation: Image-guided percutaneous coaxial core needle biopsy, 14–18 gauge, is strongly recommended [1].
sourceArticle: Management of Primary Retroperitoneal Sarcoma (RPS) in the Adult: An Updated Consensus Approach from the Transatlantic Australasian RPS Working Group

question: When may biopsy be omitted?

options.A: When an expert finds the imaging pathognomonic, such as heterogeneous dedifferentiated or well-differentiated liposarcoma

correctAnswerText: When an expert finds the imaging pathognomonic, such as heterogeneous dedifferentiated or well-differentiated liposarcoma
explanation: Biopsy may occasionally be omitted when imaging is judged pathognomonic by an expert, with dedifferentiated or well-differentiated liposarcoma given as the example [1].
sourceArticle: Management of Primary Retroperitoneal Sarcoma (RPS) in the Adult: An Updated Consensus Approach from the Transatlantic Australasian RPS Working Group

question: What did STRASS change?

options.A: Routine neoadjuvant radiotherapy is not recommended, based on abdominal recurrence-free survival
options.D: The trial supported radiotherapy for every subtype

correctAnswerText: Routine neoadjuvant radiotherapy is not recommended, based on abdominal recurrence-free survival
explanation: Based on the primary endpoint of abdominal recurrence-free survival, routine use of neoadjuvant radiotherapy is not recommended [1].
sourceArticle: Management of Primary Retroperitoneal Sarcoma (RPS) in the Adult: An Updated Consensus Approach from the Transatlantic Australasian RPS Working Group

question: About half of retroperitoneal sarcomas are:
explanation: Low- and intermediate-grade liposarcoma make up the histologic subtypes of about one-half of retroperitoneal sarcomas [1].
sourceArticle: Management of Primary Retroperitoneal Sarcoma (RPS) in the Adult: An Updated Consensus Approach from the Transatlantic Australasian RPS Working Group
